name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.isIrreducible_pureState_gnsStarAlgHom
title: The GNS representation of a pure state is irreducible

content.display_title: The GNS representation of a pure state is irreducible
content.one_sentence_role: Applies the cyclic pure-state criterion to the space and vector constructed from the same state.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra, and let $\varphi$ be a pure state: a positive normalized continuous complex-linear functional extreme in the real state space. Let $(H_\varphi,\rho_\varphi,\xi_\varphi)$ be its GNS representation. Then the only closed reducing subspaces of $H_\varphi$ for $\rho_\varphi$ are $0$ and $H_\varphi$.
content.assumptions: The representation and space in the conclusion are the canonical GNS construction from $\varphi$, not an independently chosen representation on an arbitrary Hilbert space. No separability hypothesis is present.
content.conclusion: The canonical GNS star-algebra homomorphism is irreducible. Its norm-one cyclic vector also ensures that its Hilbert space is nonzero.
content.proof_summary: Verify the norm, cyclicity and pure vector-functional hypotheses of the cyclic irreducibility criterion.
proof_steps: The GNS construction for the positive functional underlying $\varphi$ supplies $$\|\xi_\varphi\|=1,\qquad \overline{\{\rho_\varphi(a)\xi_\varphi:a\in A\}}=H_\varphi.$$ Normalization $\varphi(1)=1$ gives the first equation; cyclicity of the construction gives the second.

For every $a\in A$, the GNS inner-product identity is $$\langle\xi_\varphi,\rho_\varphi(a)\xi_\varphi\rangle=\varphi(a).$$ Hence the entire vector functional of $\xi_\varphi$ equals the same pure state $\varphi$, rather than merely agreeing at the unit.

Apply [Cyclic pure vector states force irreducibility](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/State/Irreducible.lean#L22-L125) with $\rho_\varphi$ and $\xi_\varphi$. Step 1 verifies the norm-one and dense-orbit inputs; Step 2 transports the given purity to its vector-functional input. The output is exactly irreducibility of $\rho_\varphi$.

To see the mechanism of the criterion, let $K\subseteq H_\varphi$ be a closed reducing subspace, and let $P$ be its orthogonal projection. Then $P^*=P=P^2$ and $P\rho_\varphi(a)=\rho_\varphi(a)P$ for every $a$. Define the positive functional $$\psi(a)=\langle P\xi_\varphi,\rho_\varphi(a)P\xi_\varphi\rangle.$$ Orthogonality of $K$ and $K^\perp$, and invariance of both, give $$\varphi(a)=\psi(a)+\langle(I-P)\xi_\varphi,\rho_\varphi(a)(I-P)\xi_\varphi\rangle.$$ Hence $0\le\psi(a)\le\varphi(a)$ for every positive $a$. Apply [A positive functional dominated by a pure state](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/State/Purity.lean#L38-L44) to the given pure $\varphi$ and this $\psi$: there is $t\in[0,1]$ such that $\psi=t\varphi$.

For arbitrary $a,b\in A$, self-adjointness and idempotence of $P$, followed by its commutation with the representation, yield $$\begin{aligned}\langle\rho_\varphi(a)\xi_\varphi,P\rho_\varphi(b)\xi_\varphi\rangle&=\langle P\rho_\varphi(a)\xi_\varphi,P\rho_\varphi(b)\xi_\varphi\rangle\\&=\langle\rho_\varphi(a)P\xi_\varphi,\rho_\varphi(b)P\xi_\varphi\rangle\\&=\psi(a^*b)=t\varphi(a^*b)\\&=t\langle\rho_\varphi(a)\xi_\varphi,\rho_\varphi(b)\xi_\varphi\rangle.\end{aligned}$$ Here the inner product is linear in its second argument. For fixed $b$, density of the vectors $\rho_\varphi(a)\xi_\varphi$ makes $P\rho_\varphi(b)\xi_\varphi=t\rho_\varphi(b)\xi_\varphi$. Density in $b$ and continuity now give $P=tI$ on all of $H_\varphi$.

Finally $P^2=P$ implies $(t^2-t)\xi_\varphi=0$. The norm-one vector $\xi_\varphi$ is nonzero, so $t^2=t$ and $t\in\{0,1\}$. Thus $P=0$ or $P=I$, and its range $K$ is respectively $0$ or $H_\varphi$, as required.
